title: eludite.forge.branch_from_issue input
description: Create a branch for an issue (the Issues window's Create Branch): `issue/<n>-<slug of the title>` (or `name`) from `base` (default the current branch's commit) through eludite.git's branch path, checked out unless `checkout` is false, and the link recorded on the forge where it supports linking (GitHub's development panel, GitLab's related branch through a note, Azure DevOps' work item branch link, Forgejo's branch reference, a comment on Tangled). For an agent, under the solution policy's `forge.write`: `prompt` (the default) makes the first write of an agent session dangerous (the Agents window asks; "Allow for this session" holds until the session ends), `allow` runs it, `deny` refuses it. The repository is the workspace's (its remote `origin`, or `remote`), detected as eludite.forge.detect does; every call runs on the forge worker off the UI thread with a timeout and stops when canceled. A call that needs a token when none is stored for the host fails with `sign_in_required: <host>`: the person signs in (Git > Sign in to <forge>); an agent cannot.
x-eludite-escalates: Execute; For an agent, under the solution policy's `forge.write`: `prompt` (the default) makes the first write of an agent session dangerous (the Agents window asks; "Allow for this session" holds until the session ends), `allow` runs it, `deny` refuses it.

number.description: The number (GitHub, GitLab's `iid`, Azure DevOps, Forgejo, Gitea). Give `number` or `id`.

id.description: The item's `id` as a list answered it; Tangled's items have only this (their AT-URI). Give `number` or `id`.

remote.description: The git remote to read (default `origin`, else the only remote).

link.description: Record the link on the forge (default true).
